time_to_line_crossing — DRIVE lateral op

• Data kinds: none → scalar (an op determined by its arguments alone — it takes no image or data input)

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.time_to_line_crossing(offset: 'float', heading_error: 'float', curvature: 'float', speed: 'float', *, line_offset: 'float', lane_curvature: 'float' = 0.0) -> 'float' (to call the implementation directly, import drivelateral; drivelateral.time_to_line_crossing(offset: 'float', heading_error: 'float', curvature: 'float', speed: 'float', *, line_offset: 'float', lane_curvature: 'float' = 0.0) -> 'float'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("time_to_line_crossing"))

Usage

TLC: time [s] until the vehicle (its reference point) reaches the lane boundary, assuming it drives a circle (or straight line) at its current curvature.

Coordinates: origin at a point on the lane centreline, +x along the centreline direction, +y to the left. The car is at (0, offset), with heading relative to the centreline heading_error and curvature curvature (left is positive). The boundary is the line offset laterally by line_offset (left is positive) from the centreline —— if the centreline is a circle of curvature lane_curvature, it is the circle concentric with it. If it is not reached, inf.

Raises ValueError: non-finite, v ≤ 0, the car is already outside the boundary (judged from the relation between offset and line_offset).
